clue.text: Ornamentation built of stone

indicators.note: something built is put together from raw material, so the letters are assembled into a new form

blocks.note: the seven letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Decorative carving made from stone, as on a cathedral facade.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a decorative garland or carved swag of flowers hung in a curve, a classic piece of ornament.

clue.text: Ringing diatribe over turned up nose

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning a word up means reading it from the bottom upwards
one thing lying over another can cover it on both sides, wrapping round it

blocks.note: a rant is a long angry tirade
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loudly ranting about a turned-up, snooty nose.
explanation.walkthrough: A turned-up nose sounds like snobbery in the surface; in a down clue it simply means the word is written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is deep, echoing and sustained, much like a bell that keeps on ringing.

clue.text: Region affected by herpes outbreak

indicators.note: an outbreak is a sudden breaking out, so the letters burst apart and regroup

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An area of the country hit by an epidemic of a viral infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere can mean a field or area of influence or activity, as in a sphere of operations.

clue.text: To pass through Cockney territory you need a weapon

blocks.note: to cross a place is to pass through or over it
Bow is a district of East London, Cockney heartland

explanation.surface: A traveller warned that crossing the East End requires arming yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: A true Cockney is said to be born within the sound of Bow Bells, so Bow stands for Cockney territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow mounted on a stock that shoots bolts, a medieval missile weapon.

clue.text: Shy, retiring - youth leader material

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for shy is read backwards
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: timid means shy or nervous
the opening letter of youth

explanation.surface: A bashful, self-effacing head of a youth group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy, retiring' reads as two adjectives for a person; retiring is actually the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimity is a light, sheer cotton fabric woven with raised stripes or checks, used for curtains and dresses.

clue.text: Protective gear used to fight to hold post

definitions.note: describes the thing by its function rather than naming it

blocks.note: chain mail is armour worn for protection
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Armour worn in combat to defend a military position.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'post' a military position to be held; here it is letters arriving by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailbox is a receptacle where delivered letters and parcels are kept until collected.

clue.text: It's right to keep a bit back to have something for the auditor

indicators.note: going back means the word for a bit is read from its end to its start
to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: RT is a standard abbreviation for right
a piece is a bit of something

explanation.surface: Holding back a small portion so the accountant has something to check.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at an accountant holding money back; 'back' is the reversal signal and 'to keep' wraps the right abbreviation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examining accounts needs written proof of payment, and that documentary evidence is the slip given after a purchase.

clue.text: Skilled hand finds working a strain

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A skilled worker discovers that the job is a strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, and an artisan is a craftsman skilled in a trade.

clue.text: Men get a bird in trouble, but that's not the full story

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder and come out jumbled

blocks.note: the eleven letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men land a woman in difficulty, though there is more to the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a young woman, which colours the surface; here it is just four letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridgement is a shortened version of a text, so it gives a cut-down rather than complete account.

clue.text: Seizure of one of eight?

blocks.note: first meaning: a sudden medical attack caused by a blocked or burst blood vessel in the brain
second meaning: the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace for a rowing eight

explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing boat with eight oarsmen; the one who sets the rhythm takes the name of the rowing motion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an apoplectic attack and the pace-setting oarsman in a rowing crew.

clue.text: It's mean to grab the kitty and it used to mean prison

indicators.note: to grab something is to clutch it, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: base means low or contemptible
the till is where the cash kitty is kept

explanation.surface: A miser seizes the shared fund, a word with an old penal sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' appears twice: first as the wordplay adjective, then as the verb in the definition phrase. A kitty is a pool of shared cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress used as a state jail, stormed in 1789, and its name came to stand for any lock-up.

clue.text: She's about 16 1/2 feet

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the measure is read backwards

blocks.note: a rod, pole or perch is an old unit of length of five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A woman described as remarkably tall.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a giantess; the length is an imperial measure, read as 'a rod' and turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dora is a woman's name, and crosswords freely use 'she' to stand for any female first name.

clue.text: A writer could be blind, yet no different

indicators.note: making the letters different means rearranging them into another order

blocks.note: the ten letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: an author might be sightless, and yet not be so.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton was the prolific English author of children's books such as the Famous Five series.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a famous British author, so she is an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Where to lock up people with eccentric habits?

blocks.note: eccentric means odd or peculiar
habits are someone's customary ways of behaving

explanation.surface: A wry question about where society confines its oddballs.
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeways is the well-known Victorian prison in Manchester, now officially HMP Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester jail is a place for detaining convicted criminals, which is what the defining phrase describes.

clue.text: Jack takes a girl to Leatherhead - that's unusual

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman
Norma is a girl's name
the head of leather, its first letter, read out of the town's name

explanation.surface: A man escorts a woman to a Surrey town, which is out of character.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a commuter town in Surrey, but the setter splits it into a word and its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from what is typical or expected, so it is a direct synonym for strange or uncommon.

clue.text: Anxious for young to start bringing in some cash

indicators.note: placing something at the start puts it at the front of the rest

blocks.note: Y is a standard abbreviation for young
earning means bringing in money from work

explanation.surface: Eager for a teenager to begin making some money of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone longing for something is eager or desirous, the sense of 'anxious for' as in keen to have.

clue.text: Question an Anglican with suspicion

blocks.note: to ask is to question
taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Quizzing a churchgoer in a distrustful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to regard something doubtfully or with mistrust, an idiomatic adverb.

clue.text: One has to join up without becoming a fighter

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to solder is to join metal parts with molten alloy
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone must enlist in the army without actually turning into a combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' suggests enlisting; it is metalwork. I goes inside SOLD-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a member of an army, someone whose trade is combat, so a warrior or fighting man.

clue.text: It can be so romantic - really great!

indicators.note: what the letters can be is another arrangement they could form

blocks.note: the ten letters of these words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gushing that love can be so very wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomic is used informally of amounts so vast they seem measured in star distances, hence enormous.

clue.text: The making of a dynastic line?

definitions.text: The making of a dynastic line
definitions.note: a noun phrase for the act, matching the verbal noun
an adjective, as in a ruling house

blocks.clueFragment: The making of a dynastic line
blocks.note: first meaning: drawing a straight line with a ruler, here dressed up as founding a royal house
second meaning: belonging to the family that reigns, as in a governing house

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as founding a royal family; the word also means drawing lines on paper, and the adjective inside it describes a reigning dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: The verbal noun means marking straight strokes with a straightedge, and as an adjective it describes the family that governs a kingdom.

clue.text: First impressions ensured his reputation

blocks.note: surface reading: someone known for the good impact made at a first meeting
setter's reading: the man famed for producing the first printed impressions in England

explanation.walkthrough: William Caxton set up the first printing press in England in 1476; an impression is a print from type.
explanation.definitionFit: He is remembered as England's pioneering printer, and printed copies are called impressions.

clue.text: Book that's half a gram overweight

indicators.note: taking half of a word drops two of its four letters and keeps the rest

blocks.note: taken as written; only its back half is kept
OS is outsize, the clothing label for large sizes

explanation.surface: A volume that is just over the expected weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, and crosswords use 'book' for any biblical book.

clue.text: Vessel in which little Reagan's said to have been christened?

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, so we go by how they sound

blocks.note: to be christened is to be given a name
Ron is short for Ronald, Ronald Reagan's first name

explanation.surface: A joke about the font where the former US president was baptised.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'called Ron' sounds like the cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large metal pot for boiling over a fire, a kind of cooking container.

clue.text: Location of dome project

blocks.note: surface reading: the site of a modern building scheme such as London's Millennium Dome
setter's reading: the place where Kubla Khan decreed his pleasure-dome in Coleridge's poem

explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem 'Kubla Khan' opens with a stately pleasure-dome decreed there; the surface points to the controversial Millennium Dome being built when the puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the summer capital of the Mongol emperor, immortalised in verse as the site of his palace.

clue.text: Backward boys can get in disgrace

indicators.note: backward means facing the other way, so the word is read from end to start
to get in is to enter, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: lads are boys
taken as written

explanation.surface: Slow-witted lads may end up shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward boys' reads as slow children, but backward is the reversal signal applied to the word for boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an affair causing public outrage and shame, so it is a source of dishonour.

clue.text: One starts to subside

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who establishes an organisation
second meaning: to sink or collapse, as a ship or building does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person beginning to sink; in fact the two halves name opposite ideas, beginning and collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is someone who establishes an institution, and the verb means to sink, give way or fail.
